Subject: Pilot qualification: Polaris Health inference profile and performance proof pack

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the materials we promised so the team can validate fit and scope the pilot.

Short summary
- Goal: evaluate Redwood inference for Polaris Health triage assistant (clinical summarization + question answering) under a 2k-token average context.
- Recommended pilot: 2 weeks, 10 sustained QPS target with bursts to 25 QPS for short windows; include regression guards and eval hooks.

What we shared (attachments + links)
- Redwood-verified performance pack (attached) — includes TPS, p50/p95/p99 latency percentiles for the recommended model variants and test traces that match your prompt shapes.
- Prompt pack (attached) — canonical prompt templates & small prompt-set for quality regression checks.
- Benchmark traces & raw perf artifacts — Drive link in related_links.

Model recommendations (initial shortlist)
- Llama-3-13B-redwood-q4f16: good latency/cost balance for 2k context; strong quality for extractive summarization.
- Mistral-70B-compat (quantized variant): higher latency/cost but useful as a fallback for hard QA cases where extra capacity required.

Key tradeoffs and concerns
- Quality regression risk: your domain uses medical shorthand and frequent entity-preservation; our suggested eval set focuses on entity recall and hallucination detection.
- Long-context throughput: for 2k contexts we recommend prefix/KV caching for repeated patient context — we'll enable that in pilot config.

Next steps (ask)
1) Confirm pilot scope (duration/QPS) and whether you want the 70B fallback included.
2) Approve share of SOC2 checklist items so we can provision SSO and test datasets.
3) We’ll schedule a kickoff + onboarding (30–45m) to walk through prompt pack and baseline evals.

I attached the perf pack + prompt pack and a one-page pilot map. Links + HubSpot deal are below. I’ll follow up with a SOW/PO path once you confirm scope.

—
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Dec 20, 2026 at 09:12 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the materials we promised so the team can validate fit and scope the pilot.

Jordan — great questions. Short answers and exact numbers below (we validated these on a 2k-token test harness that mirrors your traces):

Quality regression detection
- We recommend three-tier monitoring during pilot:
  1) Prompt-level heuristics: token-conservation checks + hallucination heuristics (entity mismatch to source).
  2) Eval-set runs: run the included prompt_pack_v1.json (10–20 canonical cases) every 2 hours; compute quality deltas vs baseline.
  3) Alerting & rollback: set threshold (e.g., >6% drop in entity recall OR >4% increase in hallucination rate) to trigger automatic traffic shift to a conservative model variant and a paged alert to your SRE.
- We’ll wire these as part of Redwood Console (we’ll share the dashboard and alert rules link post-kickoff).

Performance (2k-token context) — verified profiles
- Llama-3-13B-redwood-q4f16 (quantized):
  • Sustained throughput: ~10–12 TPS at 2k tokens per request (config: 10 concurrent worker threads).
  • Latency percentiles: p50 ~38ms per token (~76ms request overhead), p95 ~210ms, p99 ~480ms.
  • Cost: baseline estimate ~ $0.008/token processed (example unit pricing; we’ll produce line-item in SOW).
- Mistral-70B-compat (quantized fallback):
  • Sustained throughput: ~1.5–2.5 TPS at 2k tokens.
  • Latency percentiles: p50 ~420ms, p95 ~1.8s, p99 ~3.5s.
  • Use case: edge-case QA where longer reasoning improves correctness; recommended only for a small fraction (<=5%) of traffic as a fallback.

Benchmarks / evidence
- All traces and raw logs are in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyBenchmarkTracesAndPrompts (includes the scripts we used to reproduce).
- Redwood-verified summary (human-reviewed runbook) here: https://redwood.example.com/perf/profiles/polaris-verified-2026-12

Pilot configuration suggestion (minimal)
- Duration: 2 weeks; traffic split: 95% 13B variant / 5% 70B fallback (can be tuned).
- Regression checks: run prompt_pack_v1.json every 2 hours; snapshot outputs to the evaluation table; automated alerts if thresholds exceeded.
- Ops handoff: we’ll provide a short runbook and a “preflight” checklist for your infra/procurement teams.

Next steps
- If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff with engineering + SRE. Proposed times: Tue 12/22 10:00am or Wed 12/23 2:00pm PT — which works?
- We’ll also prepare a short SOW + cost estimate for procurement to review.

—
Marissa Cole
Manager, Applied ML | Redwood Inference
